proposed_comments.title: Keep the hook active until the swallowed release is consumed

confidence.rationale: The validated fork fix showed the low-level hook must remain active while a swallowed left-button release is pending.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep the hook active until the swallowed release is consumed

**Severity:** `major`

Please keep the low-level mouse hook active while a swallowed left-button release is still pending, even after the overlay begins dismissing. Otherwise the physical `WM_LBUTTONUP` can reach the underlying application without its matching button-down. Continue routing that release through the hook and consume it before teardown.

proposed_comments.title: Do not unhook after gap or padding clicks while the overlay remains visible

confidence.rationale: The validated fork fix keeps hover/click selection working after swallowed button-up events that do not dismiss the overlay.

proposed_comments.body:
### Do not unhook after gap or padding clicks while the overlay remains visible

**Severity:** `major`

Please do not unhook the mouse hook after every swallowed button-up while the overlay remains visible. A click in tile padding or a gap can leave the overlay open; unhooking here makes later hover and click selection stop working for the rest of that session. Only tear down the hook after the overlay has been dismissed.

proposed_comments.title: Force final shutdown to clear hook state

confidence.rationale: The validated fork fix adds a final teardown path so stale hook state cannot survive shutdown while a swallowed release is pending.

proposed_comments.body:
### Force final shutdown to clear hook state

**Severity:** `major`

Please add a forced final-shutdown teardown path that always unhooks the mouse hook and clears `g_swallowedLeftDown`. If shutdown occurs while a swallowed button-up is pending, the deferred ordinary teardown can otherwise leave stale hook state and prevent a later enable from installing a new hook.
